summary.headline: EIH Q1 FY27 revenue rose 15% to Rs 698 crore and PAT to Rs 120 crore, but EBITDA grew only to Rs 207 crore as margin fell on Rajgarh ramp-up and one-offs.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 15% YoY to Rs 698 crore (Rs 609 crore) and EBITDA rose to Rs 207 crore from Rs 195 crore, so margin compressed. Management attributed the gap to Oberoi Rajgarh ramp-up, about Rs 4 crore of extra marketing, IT/automation spend, power and fuel inflation from the West Asia conflict, and Rs 6-7.5 crore of renovation write-offs at Mumbai hotels. Growth was domestically led as foreign arrivals fell about 10% in Q1. Standalone numbers were stated to mirror consolidated. PAT of Rs 120 crore is not comparable with last year, which carried a Rs 110 crore Mashobra one-time impact.

financial_highlights.change: from Rs 195 crore YoY; margin about 29% as stated
not comparable; prior year had Rs 110 crore Mashobra one-time impact

segments.name: Oberoi brand (luxury)
segments.commentary: RevPAR grew 8.2% vs luxury segment industry 13.2%; excluding Oberoi Rajgarh, RevPAR growth was 11.4%. Foreign-heavy mix was hit by West Asia conflict.

segments.name: Trident brand (upper upscale)
segments.commentary: RevPAR grew 13.8% vs industry 9.2%; Mumbai TNP and BKC drove it, Trident RGI at 162 vs 155 last year.

segments.name: Flight catering (OFS)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 154 crore in Q1, driven by new domestic flights and direct international airline business; management said it was profitable and did not materially dilute margin.

segments.name: Oberoi Rajgarh (new, Khajuraho)
segments.commentary: Opened November 2025; in ramp-up, weighing on margins. Management expects about 3 years to stabilise and stronger winter months from October.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 business on books vs last year described as very positive; no full-year guidance given.
Industry expected to see ARR gains from limited supply and MICE events (BRICS, Aviation show) later in the year.
Foreign tourist arrivals expected to normalise in Q3 and Q4 FY27 if West Asia stabilises; Q2 foreign trend expected to remain weak.
Renovations to finish before October; no significant renovation in Q3 and Q4.
Oberoi Grand (Delhi/Kolkata-listed project in pipeline) expected to open September 2028 with 197 keys.
Kolkata Oberoi timeline pushed to 2029, citing heritage restoration safety work and a construction halt in Kolkata after a fatal incident about two months earlier.
Pipeline of about 30 new properties by 2031 including managed and owned hotels; managed pipeline 23 hotels and 1,833 keys, with one property (60 keys) pushed beyond 2032.
capex_capacity: Footprint: 3,801 keys in India and 408 keys international.
Seven owned and associate pipeline hotels; The Oberoi London expected in 2028; most others domestic.
Hebbal (Bengaluru) to host an Oberoi and a Trident plus about 763,000 sq ft retail/F&B, total development area over 1.3 million sq ft.
Wildflower bid qualifying date moved from 26 August to 10 September 2026, followed by a live auction; management would not disclose bid.
Renovation capex fully capitalised; abandoned assets with residual life written off to P&L (Rs 7.5 crore in Q1 per analyst confirmation).
demand_pricing: Industry Q1: occupancy up 2-4%, ARR up 6-8%; domestic demand offset lower foreign bookings.
EIH MPI 108 (vs 106); ARI flat at 115; RGI 125 (vs 121) vs STR comp set; 14 of 15 hotels ranked 1st or 2nd.
Company RevPAR (all hotels incl. managed) rose from Rs 11,352 to Rs 12,801; owned hotels rose from about Rs 13,000 to nearly Rs 15,000 by quarter end.
Shimla and Chandigarh showed the biggest RevPAR gains (base effect from Operation Sindoor); Jaipur fell on lower foreign arrivals; Hyderabad declined against the Miss World base.
Foreign guest arrivals were about 10% below last year in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Did flight catering mix and renovation, Rajgarh ramp-up drive the margin gap, and will these persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said renovations concentrate in lean months and Bombay renovations finish before October; Rajgarh should improve in winter. Flight catering was profitable and not a material margin drag.

qa_highlights.question: May and June RevPAR growth looked much higher than the quarter. Will that persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to forecast the full year; said Q2 business on books versus last year was very positive.

qa_highlights.question: Will large events like BRICS and the Aviation show boost RevPAR?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, large events have a ripple effect across cities, with Delhi and Mumbai benefiting from overseas visitors to Bengaluru's air show.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Kolkata Oberoi delayed and how firm is the new timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Heritage building restoration uncovered fire and structural safety work, plus a Kolkata construction halt after a fatal incident about two months ago; halt still in place pending building-by-building approvals.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a cost overrun on the Oberoi Grand from delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Delays add cost, the size depending on reasons, and the bigger impact is deferred revenue and profit from delayed market entry.

qa_highlights.question: Can the Mumbai outperformance continue, and what is foreign tourist trend in recent months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Bombay market was strong and EIH beat it, but would not forecast 20% outperformance; Q2 foreign trend expected to stay weak.

qa_highlights.question: Rajgarh stabilisation timeline and winter outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: About 3 years to stabilise for a leisure hotel, with winter months from October expected to do considerably better.

qa_highlights.question: How much did the base business margin fall after adjusting for Rajgarh and one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ex-Rajgarh margin was about 30.6% vs last year, with roughly Rs 9 crore YoY impact from power and fuel, Rs 4 crore marketing, IT and renovation costs. Management declined to disclose management fee income.
